title: Start Here
subtitle: A getting-started guide to Randall Young’s Project Atlas
intro: Project Atlas is a public guide to experiments, classroom activities, instruments, and their source records. You do not need to understand the whole archive to use it. Pick one question, try one thing, and follow the evidence.

routes.title: Try something in the browser
routes.text: Pluck the virtual Singing Rule. Predict what shortening the ruler does, then test your prediction.

routes.title: Teach an inquiry lesson

exhibits.title: The Singing Rule
exhibits.text: See the original ruler and Bluetooth setup, then compare measured ringdown with a model you can pluck.
exhibits.start: Shorten the virtual ruler and predict what its frequency will do.

exhibits.title: Pop-Can Calorimeter
exhibits.text: Follow candle mass loss and water heating. Learn why fuel power and heat captured by the water are different quantities.
exhibits.start: Switch between two heating curves with equal total water heat.

exhibits.title: SQM+ Hallway Observatory
exhibits.text: Use an 11 m course to separate stopwatch speed, device recording, and experimental step detection.
exhibits.start: Change the candidate count in the calculator without changing the timed speed.

exhibits.title: Virtual Instruments

exhibits.start: Pick a voltmeter, frequency meter, scale, ToF ruler, or thermometer.

exhibits.title: Ten Problems That Teach Calculus
exhibits.text: Start with a motion problem where total distance and net change are not the same thing.
exhibits.start: Try Problem 06, then use the worked solutions or handouts.

exhibits.title: CORE 10
exhibits.text: Connect the Kitchen Inquiry Lab, One Cup Chemistry, and the Personal Energy Laboratory.
exhibits.start: Compare the energy an appliance uses with the heat gained by a cup of water.

evidence: A measured run, a simulated example, and a working dashboard are different kinds of evidence. Read the captions and validation notes before you draw a conclusion. A good first experiment is one you can explain and repeat.
